newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission hints again at BT/MCI clearance.
newsitem.headline: Commission hints again at BT/MCI clearance.

text.p: The European Commission further hinted on Wednesday that it would soon clear the $20 billion merger between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Corp of the United States.

"(European Competition Comissioner Karel) Van Miert has said publicly that if the conditions are going to be met, and apparently it's more than the case, we'll be able to clear it," Van Miert's spokesman told a news briefing in reply to a question.

The spokesman also said that the partnership between BT, MCI and Telefonica de Espana would have to be submitted to the EU for clearance under article 85 of the treaty of Rome, which bans agreements or restrictive practices that harm fair competition.
BT announced on Friday it had brought Telefonica into its alliance with MCI by taking a two percent stake in the Spanish company. Telefonica would in return buy a one percent holding in BT.

The Telefonica deal, as well as an agreement with Portugal Telecom announced earlier this week, do not fall under the EU's fast-track merger regulation because they do not involve BT taking control of the Iberian companies.
Article 85 investigations are usually lengthy, depending on the companies' willingness to cooperate with the Commission. In the Telefonica case, contacts have already taken place.
"Mr Van Miert has been informed at the highest level by BT of its intentions," the spokesman said in reply to questions.
Telefonica's alliance with BT throws into question the Unisource deal with AT&T, the Swiss telecoms operator, PTT Telecom of the Netherlands and Sweden's Telia.

The Commission announced in December it would clear the Unisource alliance after long and difficult negotiations with the Spanish government which resulted in the early liberalisation of the country's telecoms market.

On the much bigger alliance between BT and MCI, Commission sources have said that clearance hinges on access to the two partners' transatlantic cable capacity and BT's position in the British market for teleconferencing.
The deadline for the EU to give its final verdict is June 11, but Commission officials say clearance could come in the first half of May.
